ch2_p6_neyman_sim_solo.text: Welcome to the Neyman Optimal Allocation Workbench. Adjust stratum sample standard deviations and watch how Jerzy Neyman's formula dynamically shifts sample sizes away from low-variance strata and into high-variance strata, minimizing global estimator variance.

ch2_p6_neyman_sim_duo.text: Check out the Neyman Allocation Workbench! Drag the Rural standard deviation slider up to 42. Notice how Neyman more than doubles its sample allocation compared to proportional sampling, achieving a twenty percent variance reduction for free!

ch2_p6_chk1_solo.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 1. Under what mathematical condition is the Horvitz-Thompson estimator guaranteed to be strictly unbiased for the true population total Y?

ch2_p6_chk1_duo.text: Active Checkpoint 1! Remember Dr. Nova's proof on Slide 3. What must be true about the inclusion probability pi-sub-i for every single unit in the target population?

ch2_p6_chk1_feedback_correct.text: Outstanding! Option B is correct. The Horvitz-Thompson estimator is strictly unbiased if and only if every element in the target population has a strictly positive selection probability, pi-sub-i greater than zero. If any population subset has pi-sub-i equal to zero, that group suffers permanent under-coverage, resulting in irrecoverable sampling bias.

ch2_p6_chk1_feedback_incorrect.text: Not quite. Remember our expectation derivation: expected value of Y-hat Horvitz-Thompson equals the sum of y-sub-i divided by pi-sub-i times expected value of the indicator I-sub-i, which is pi-sub-i. If any unit has pi-sub-i equal to zero, the denominator is undefined and that subgroup is permanently excluded. The correct answer is Option B.

ch2_p6_cluster_deff_sim_solo.text: Welcome to the Cluster Sampling and Kish's Design Effect Simulator. Explore how cluster size m and intra-class correlation rho interact to inflate estimator variance and diminish effective independent observations.

ch2_p6_cluster_deff_sim_duo.text: Let us test Kish's Design Effect! Drag the cluster size slider m past 30 and watch how quickly intra-cluster correlation erodes your effective sample size. That is why sampling smaller clusters across more sites is almost always superior!

ch2_p6_chk2_solo.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 2. A market research team samples 50 retail stores and interviews 20 customers per store, with an intra-cluster correlation of 0.15. For a total interviewed sample of 1,000, what is the Design Effect Deff and the effective sample size n-effective?

ch2_p6_chk2_duo.text: Active Checkpoint 2! Apply Kish's formula: Deff equals 1 plus m minus 1 times rho. Cluster size m is 20, and rho is 0.15. Calculate Deff, then divide 1,000 by Deff to find the effective sample size!

ch2_p6_chk2_feedback_correct.text: Spot on! Option C is correct. Deff equals 1 plus 20 minus 1 times 0.15, which is 1 plus 19 times 0.15, giving 1 plus 2.85, or exactly 3.85. Dividing total sample size 1,000 by 3.85 yields an effective sample size of approximately 260 independent observations. Despite interviewing 1,000 shoppers, customer correlation within the same store cuts statistical precision by nearly three-quarters.

ch2_p6_chk2_feedback_incorrect.text: Incorrect. Be careful with the arithmetic in Leslie Kish's formula: Deff equals 1 plus m minus 1 times rho. With m equal to 20, m minus 1 is 19. Multiplying 19 by 0.15 gives 2.85, and adding 1 gives a Deff of 3.85. Dividing 1,000 by 3.85 gives approximately 260. The correct answer is Option C.
